position: Jennifer Hazelton (pp. 724-727), who argues for keeping and using EXIM against China. The opposing essay by Veronique de Rugy (pp. 717-724) argues for abolition and is tracked as c23-01.
proposal: Jennifer Hazelton's essay argues that the United States should keep a functioning Export-Import Bank because China uses state-backed export credit as a strategic tool and other countries' export credit agencies have adapted, in some cases by lowering domestic content requirements. She presents EXIM as the only American vehicle that can provide the sovereign-backed financing some projects require and does not specify statutory changes.

status_summary: EXIM remains in operation, and its charter and its China and Transformational Exports Program (CTEP) run through 2026-12-31. The Senate confirmed John Jovanovic as President and Chair on 2025-09-18; CRS reports $8.7 billion in FY2025 authorizations and a board-approved loan of up to $10 billion for the Project Vault critical-minerals reserve announced 2026-02-02, and EXIM's newsroom lists new financings through 2026-10-06. Reauthorization is pending: S. 3772 would extend the charter 10 years and a House Financial Services discussion draft of March 2026 would extend it 5 years, but a CRS report of 2026-05-07 and a trade summary of 2026-08-21 report no markup or vote. The FY2027 request seeks a $200 million program budget against $20 million enacted for FY2026. The text of S. 3772 (introduced 2026-02-04 by Sen. Cramer with Sen. Warner) extends the charter by ten years through date changes only; the House Financial Services Committee's full committee markups of 2026-05-13, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-16 list no EXIM measure; and the continuing appropriations act signed 2026-09-02 (H.R. 6500, Public Law 119-103) contains no EXIM provision.

timeline.event: The Senate confirms John Jovanovic as EXIM President and Chair (term to 2029-01-20); the board has two vacancies against a three-member quorum.

EXIM's FY2025 ends with $8.7 billion in new authorizations (supporting an estimated $10.1 billion in export sales), a portfolio exposure of $34.8 billion against a $135 billion cap, and a default rate of 1.023 percent, per CRS.
Project Vault, a critical-minerals reserve, is announced, backed by a board-approved EXIM direct loan of up to $10 billion with about $2 billion in private capital.

Sen. Cramer, with Sen. Warner as an original cosponsor, introduces S. 3772, the Export-Import Bank Reauthorization Act of 2026, referred to the Senate Banking Committee; its only changes are date amendments that extend the Bank's authority from 2026 to 2036, its loan, guarantee and insurance authority date from 2027 to 2037, and the China and Transformational Exports Program dates from 2026 to 2036.

A House Financial Services subcommittee holds a hearing and the Senate Banking Committee holds a hearing on reauthorization in March 2026; a House discussion draft would extend the charter and CTEP five years, extend the exposure cap four years, and add nuclear energy to CTEP. The Senate Banking Committee's own listing dates its hearing 'Export-Import Bank Reauthorization' to 2026-03-26.

The Senate Banking Committee holds a full committee hearing titled 'Export-Import Bank Reauthorization' (the committee's hearing listing gives the title only; its listing for later 2026 hearings through 2026-10-01 shows no further Export-Import Bank hearing, and markups were not checked).
timeline.source: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

timeline.event: A legislative-news summary reports S. 3772 (10-year extension) and the House discussion draft, with no markup, committee vote or floor vote reported, and notes that a lapse would stop new transactions after 2026-12-31.
EXIM announces that it has returned to profitability, in a release giving no figures and not mentioning reauthorization.
timeline.source: Export-Import Bank of the United States

timeline.event: A legislative-news summary lists S. 4781, S. 5254 (civil nuclear energy in CTEP) and S. 4228 alongside the House draft, again with no markups or votes reported, and the authority still set to expire 2026-12-31.

The House Financial Services Committee's full committee markups of 2026-05-13, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-16 list no measure concerning the Export-Import Bank (the 2026-09-16 agenda is at the linked page); the enrolled Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500, signed 2026-09-02) contains no Export-Import Bank provision, so the charter remains set to expire on 2026-12-31 (other House committee markups were not checked).

EXIM reports that its Chairman joined the President in the Oval Office to announce a planned $15 billion steel plant in Iowa, after EXIM's Board approved a $770 million direct loan the week before for the supplier iron ore mine in Minnesota (the release records no presidential statement about reauthorization).
EXIM announces a $547 million loan guarantee for a proposed cable plant in Texas; its newsroom listing shows other 2026 financings and no release on reauthorization.
timeline.source: Export-Import Bank of the United States

title: Keep and reauthorize the Export-Import Bank as a counter-China export credit tool
uncertainties: Reauthorization status after 2026-08-21: pass 5 found no EXIM item on the House Financial Services full committee markup of 2026-09-16, none in the enrolled H.R. 6500, and no Senate Banking hearing after 2026-03-26 in its listing, but Senate Banking markups and other House markups were not checked, so congressional action in September or early October 2026 cannot be ruled out. The CRS report was read in part (the last portion of the page was not retrieved) and two Legis1 summaries are secondary and do not name sponsors. The Hazelton essay has no concrete statutory asks, so 'direct' match and the progress number rest on reading its position as keep-and-use. The date of the board's CTEP content policy (51 percent U.S. content for full financing) is not stated by CRS, so it is not counted as a 2025 or 2026 action. Some titles above are descriptive labels for pages whose exact headlines were not shown.
